newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares trickle lower, Mideast bank higher.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares trickle lower, Mideast bank higher.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange fell fractionally again on Monday in quiet trade despite healthy interest in Middle East Investment Bank.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell 0.09 points to 147.54 points, maintaining its shallow slide in a becalmed market from just under 148 points at the start of the month.

But expectations of a private share placement with a French bank spurred trading in MEIB, brokers said. The bank's stock rose 0.05 dinars to 1.10 after shares worth 90,500 dinars ($128,000) changed hands, making it the day's busiest share.
"Generally the picture is not changing," one broker said. "Most investors are still steering clear."
Another gaining stock was Livestock and Poultry, which rose 0.03 dinars to close at 0.57 dinar after shares worth 30,000 dinars were traded.
Brokers say the share, which soared close to one dinar in September before tumbling again, may now be undervalued.
"There has been a lot of talk that the new (company) board is prepared to get this company moving," said one broker.
But, in a sign of the sluggish trade on the Amman bourse, blue chip Arab Bank Group, frequently the busiest share on the exchange, did not trade a single share.
"There was demand at 245 dinars and supply stayed at 248," said one broker.
Overall 14 shares rose and 10 fell, with another 11 trading but closing unchanged.
